title: Capital Gains on Property
shortAnswer: Calculate tax on sale of land or building.
longAnswer: Capital gains on the sale of immovable property depend on the holding period. Under the current rules, property held for more than 24 months is a long-term asset; 24 months or less is short-term. Long-term gains are taxed at 12.5% without indexation (the indexation benefit was withdrawn for transfers on or after 23 July 2024), while short-term gains are added to your income and taxed at slab rates. Certain exemptions survive—Section 54 (reinvest in a residential house), Section 54EC (bonds), and Section 54F (reinvest in a house from other assets). The calculator takes your sale price, cost of acquisition, improvement cost, and holding period to show whether the gain is long-term or short-term and the estimated tax. Stamp duty and transfer expenses are added to the cost. TDS under Section 194IA (1% on sales above ₹50 lakh) is deducted by the buyer and can be claimed as a credit. Confirm the exact treatment with a chartered accountant.
